opus.why: The fix is fully specified: make the glow nearly transparent and about 3x wider on every dark logo example. It's a mechanical CSS/SVG edit across known pages, then opening the page.

fable.why: Mechanical style edit with a precise spec (wider, near-transparent glow) applied across all dark logo instances plus opening the page. Needs careful find-all discipline, not deep brand judgment.

opus.why: A brand book scene and t2i prompt that must follow the brand's own composition rule, plus an explanation of the changes. Visual judgment the audience will see, though the direction is well specified.

fable.why: Rewriting a brand-book hero scene and t2i prompt against written composition rules, then justifying each change. Visual/brand judgment where the owner checks against the rulebook; a weaker rewrite would show.

opus.why: A final brand book page that designers will use. It needs sound clear-space logic tied to the mark and realistic minimum sizes, written tight and practical.

fable.why: Standard clear-space/min-size brand book page with well-known conventions. Final copy designers read, but the content is formulaic and Sonnet at high produces it at full quality.

opus.why: Revising key visual prompts from art-direction notes, including two redos for composition and warmth. Visual judgment in brand output, but each note gives clear direction.

fable.why: Revising key-visual generation prompts from terse review notes requires inferring composition, warmth, and typography fixes while preserving what works. Brand visual judgment on hero assets.

opus.why: A brand palette decision that weighs the logo on dark backgrounds, clashes with the green/amber/red status colors and WCAG contrast. Judgment matters, and the answer is short.

fable.why: A real brand decision: weighing mark legibility, status-color collisions (teal vs green, coral vs red), and WCAG on dark mode. Nuanced visual reasoning with a concise recommendation.

opus.why: Composition direction for a keyframe. It needs careful spatial staging (3/4 facing, table orientation, guest placement) so the image model gets it right this time.

fable.why: Short rewrite of one keyframe composition with the fix already specified (hosts at 3/4 to camera, guest left). Needs clear visual direction but no open-ended judgment.

opus.why: CSS break-avoid rules, an automated check that finds hanging headings in the built PDF, and a global text replacement. Moderate coding work with a few parts, no deep design judgment.

fable.why: Agentic coding: add widows/orphans and break-after CSS rules, build a post-PDF check for stranded headings, and do a text replacement. Moderately tricky but well-specified; Sonnet high handles it.

opus.why: Three original launch key visual concepts with full art direction, layouts for three crops and t2i prompts, explicitly meant to make people stop. High-stakes creative brand work.

fable.why: Open-ended creative concepting: three distinctive, non-generic key visuals with full composition, light, multi-crop layout, and t2i prompts. Originality and visual taste are the deliverable.

opus.why: Brand book content: guidance for busy photo backgrounds, video safe zones and co-branding rules, plus a drawable example description for each don't. Designers use this directly.

fable.why: Extending a misuse page with standard cases (busy photo backgrounds, video safe zones, co-branding lockup rules) plus example-image descriptions. Conventional brand guidance Sonnet knows well.
